mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision point reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows over the next 60-day horizon, generating negative S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar high-inflation regimes, or FEDFUNDS decline sharply within 2 weeks after trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which crowds out risk assets and pushes S&P 500 20-day forward returns negative.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns turn positive in >50% of tight-labor periods, or employment growth decelerates while unemployment rises.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly retail sales (not in observable list, so skip) — instead: A simultaneous surge in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) above trend implies expanding economic demand, which elevates equity valuations and drives positive 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in >40% of high-INDPRO months, or both INDPRO and HOUST remain below their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 105 for three consecutive months indicates softening supply constraints, which reduces future growth expectations and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO recovers to >105 within 2 months, and 20-day returns are positive in >60% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) crosses above 5% from below, it often coincides with a pause in rate hikes and higher risk aversion, pushing 60-day S&P 500 forward returns into negative territory.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive in >75% of post-5% unemployment episodes, or rate cuts are immediately followed by strong returns.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising pay growth (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggest wage compression, which reduces equity risk premia and yields positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases month-over-month while CPIAUCSL increases by <0.5%
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >50% of months with similar wage and inflation dynamics.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time spike in consumer confidence (not observable) — instead: A sharp increase in retail sales proxies (none available) — instead: A surge in monthly personal consumption expenditures (not available) — instead: A concurrent rise in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) above the prior month's levels indicates accelerating demand, pushing 5-day S&P 500 forward returns positive.
candidate_trigger: both INDPRO and HOUST increase by >5% month-over-month
failure_condition: 5-day returns fail to beat the prior month's average in >80% of similar demand surges.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of declining inflation (CPIAUCSL < 237 for two months) and stable federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS), the S&P 500 tends to exhibit higher 20-day forward returns due to reduced discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 237 for 2 consecutive months and FEDFUNDS remains < 4.25%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >60% of low-inflation steady periods, or FEDFUNDS rises sharply while CPIAUCSL remains low.
